Include a large generated board preview as the focal area, a structured rule editor panel, controls for board size and initial layout, a few rule toggles or parameter fields, a compact validation summary, and prominent Generate Board and Start Game actions. Put strong emphasis on making complex configuration approachable through hierarchy, grouping, feedback, and a polished tabletop-tool identity.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The board preview, rule editor, size/layout controls, and toggles are all present and well-built, but two required elements are absent from the visible main screen — the compact validation summary and the prominent Generate Board / Start Game actions. The only visible action is the low-emphasis 'Reset layout' in the header, so the two most important verbs of the brief are below the fold in a scrolling rail. There is also a conceptual conflict: the preview is labeled 'LIVE PREVIEW · AUTO-GENERATED' and the header says 'All changes saved,' which undercuts what an explicit 'Generate Board' action is supposed to do. Clarity & Hierarchy: The board is the clear focal point, but it is clipped — the 9×9 grid shows rows 1–8 with row 8 cut and row 9 hidden, so the hero artifact never fully resolves on screen. The gray pill bars beside section headers 01/02/03 read as dead skeleton loaders with no explained meaning, adding noise. Interdependencies (Aspect ratio × Board shape × Grid dimensions, Objective count × seed) produce no visible feedback about conflicts or results. The right rail is also cut mid-card (Fog of war / Sight radius), so the reading flow ends abruptly. Visual System & Craft: The teal/gold dark palette, serif display type, and monospace labels form a cohesive tabletop system, and tile glyphs, legend, and coordinate grid are crisp. Weaknesses: the focal board overflows its frame instead of scaling to fit; the unexplained section pills break the otherwise precise component language; the legend floats top-right with weak association to the tiles; the rule cards' gold left borders and toggles are good but the panel below the fold is never seen, so the system's completeness can't be judged. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: 'The Gilded Reef' theme, ocean tile glyphs, and gold objective stars give real identity, but the right rail is a fairly generic dark dashboard, and there is no memorable authored moment (no validation personality, no game-start flourish, no tabletop materiality on the primary actions).
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all CSS-only, no external assets): 1) Restore the omitted brief content with a sticky footer pinned to the bottom of the right rail: 'Start Game' as the primary gold-filled CTA and 'Generate Board' as a secondary gold-outline action, always visible without scrolling; directly above it, add the compact validation summary as a slim monospace strip (e.g., '✓ 4 checks · ⚠ 1 warning: objectives exceed reef tiles') with pass/warn/fail icon states and a left accent border matching the rule cards. 2) Make the board fully fit the viewport: size tiles from available panel height (contain) so all 9 rows plus A–I/1–9 coordinates render inside the frame, and add a small 'Fit / 100%' zoom control in the preview header; move the legend to a footer strip under the board for tighter association. 3) Resolve the live-preview vs. Generate tension: keep live re-render for terrain/layout params, but have 'Generate Board' re-roll/commit the seed with a brief tile regeneration animation and flip a status chip from 'Live preview' to 'Board locked'; let 'Start Game' be the single primary verb, and update the header status ('All changes saved' → 'Ready to play') to reflect state. 4) Give the ambiguous section pills a real job — fill them as section-required fields validate (with a tooltip) — or remove them to cut noise. 5) Add interactive feedback to the preview: hover highlight on tiles with a coordinate/terrain tooltip, and a visible conflict state (e.g., red ring on the Shape control when Hex + 9×9 is invalid) so complex configuration reads as safe to touch. 6) Push tabletop distinctiveness on the new CTAs and panel header with CSS-only materiality (gold-foil gradient on Start Game, subtle grain/wood gradient on the Blueprint header) so the primary actions feel like part of the game world rather than a dashboard.
